title: Order Refunds on Orders Paid With Cartwise Gift Cards — Ledger Note
content:
When an order paid partly or wholly by a Cartwise Gift Cards card is refunded, the refund goes back to the card, up to the amount that card paid on that order, and the card is refunded before the order's other payment methods, on every card type whose setting returns order refunds to the card.

## Ledger treatment

**Return to the card.** The refund returns to the card that paid the order. The amount returned to that card is capped at the amount the card paid on that same order. The return books onto the card as a reversed redemption, tied to the refunded order and to the order refund entry it returns.

**Card first.** Gift cards are refunded before the order's other payment methods.

**Expired or closed card.** When the card that paid the order has expired or closed, the refund goes where the card type's destination setting after expiry or closure says: to the original card, or to Cartwise credit.

**Once per refund entry.** Each order refund entry is returned to a card once. Whether an entry has already been returned is read from the card's own record: a reversed redemption already booked against that same order refund entry means the entry has been returned.

## Checks on one order refund entry

| Question | Where it is answered | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Did a gift card pay part or all of the order? | The card's redemptions against that order | If yes, the refund goes back to that card first. |
| How much did that card pay on that order? | The card's redemption against that order | The return to the card does not exceed that amount. |
| Is the card expired or closed? | The card's status | If so, the card type's destination setting after expiry or closure decides where the refund goes. |
| Has this refund entry already been returned to a card? | Reversed redemptions booked against that refund entry | An entry already returned is not returned again. |

## Worked ledger examples (hypothetical inputs)

**Example 1 — refund larger than the card's share.** An order was paid 60.00 by an active gift card and 40.00 by another payment method. A single order refund of 70.00 is booked. The card is refunded first, up to the 60.00 it paid on the order, so the card receives 60.00; the remaining 10.00 falls to the order's other payment method.

**Example 2 — refund smaller than the card's share.** The same order receives instead a single refund of 25.00. The card is refunded first and 25.00 is within the 60.00 it paid, so the whole 25.00 returns to the card.

**Example 3 — the same refund entry a second time.** A reversed redemption already stands on the card for a given order refund entry. That entry is not returned to a card again.

**Example 4 — closed card.** The card that paid the order has closed, and its card type's destination setting after expiry or closure is Cartwise credit. The refund goes to Cartwise credit rather than to the card.
